===== chart.py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Year': [2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023],
    'Nordic': [18.9, 19.1, 19.3, 19.5, 19.6, 20.2, 20.5, 20.7, 20.9],
    'Sub-Saharan Africa': [10.2, 10.5, 10.8, 11.0, 11.2, 11.5, 11.8, 12.0, 12.2],
    'South Asia': [9.7, 9.9, 10.1, 10.3, 10.5, 10.8, 11.0, 11.2, 11.5],
    'Latin America': [14.5, 14.8, 15.0, 15.3, 15.6, 15.9, 16.2, 16.5, 16.8],
    'Balkans': [12.8, 13.0, 13.2, 13.4, 13.6, 13.9, 14.1, 14.3, 14.6],
    'Anglosphere': [17.6, 17.8, 18.0, 18.2, 18.4, 18.7, 19.0, 19.2, 19.5],
    'East Asia': [16.7, 16.9, 17.1, 17.3, 17.5, 17.8, 18.0, 18.3, 18.6],
    'Southeast Asia': [12.0, 12.2, 12.4, 12.6, 12.8, 13.1, 13.3, 13.5, 13.8]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df.set_index('Year', inplace=True)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
colors = [
    '#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728',
    '#9467bd', '#8c564b', '#e377c2', '#7f7f7f', '#bcbd22'
]

plt.stackplot(
    df.index,
    df['Nordic'],
    df['Sub-Saharan Africa'],
    df['South Asia'],
    df['Latin America'],
    df['Balkans'],
    df['Anglosphere'],
    df['East Asia'],
    df['Southeast Asia'],
    labels=df.columns,
    colors=colors,
    alpha=0.8
)

plt.title('Trends in Regional Social Spending (2015-2023)', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Year', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Social Spending (% of GDP)', fontsize=12)
plt.legend(loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), fontsize=10)
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png')

===== summary.txt
The image is an area chart titled "Trends in Regional Social Spending (2015-2023)," which illustrates the progression of total social spending as a percentage of GDP across nine different regions over a nine-year period. The x-axis represents the years from 2015 to 2023, while the y-axis measures total social spending as a percentage of GDP, ranging from 0% to approximately 130%.

Each region is represented by a distinct color in the stacked area chart, allowing for a clear visual comparison of their contributions to overall social spending over time. The Nordic region, depicted in blue, consistently holds the largest share, starting at around 18.9% in 2015 and gradually increasing to 20.9% by 2023. Directly above the Nordic region, the Anglosphere, shown in brown, starts at 17.6% in 2015 and rises to 19.5% by 2023. East Asia, represented in light purple, follows a similar upward trend, starting at 16.7% and reaching 18.6% in 2023.

Latin America, colored in red, begins at 14.5% in 2015 and increases to 16.8% by 2023. The Balkans, shown in grayish-purple, start at 12.8% and rise to 14.6%. Southeast Asia, in light gray, shows a rise from 12.0% to 13.8% over the same period. Sub-Saharan Africa, depicted in orange, starts at 10.2% and increases to 12.2%. South Asia, in green, begins at 9.7% and reaches 11.5% by 2023.

The chart effectively displays how each region's social spending as a percentage of GDP has grown steadily over the years, with the cumulative total of all regions depicted reaching just above 130% of GDP by 2023. The use of a grid with dashed lines aids in reading the values more precisely, while the legend, positioned outside the main plot area, helps in identifying each region by its corresponding color.
